title: Documentation
projectsBody: Create a project from the Projects page. The name starts as Name and is selected, so typing replaces it. Start with a Customers table adds a People table with Name, Mail, and one sample row. Open a project to edit its description. Right-click a project to rename or delete it.
tablesBody: A table is a grid of columns and rows. Add a column with the + at the end of the header or between two headers, and choose the type before it is created. Drag a grip to reorder a column or a row. Sort and filter from the column header; those choices stay with your account. Select rows or columns to duplicate, color, or delete them. The bar at the bottom of the grid closes with X.
formulasIntro: A formula uses a column name, or Table.Column for a column on another table. Arithmetic uses + - * / and %. Comparisons use = <> > < >= <=. Do not put = in front of the formula. Text belongs in quotes.
lookupBody: LOOKUP(Customers.Email, Email, Customers.Name) searches Customers.Email for the Email on this row and returns the Name from the matching row. The first and third arguments are columns on the same table. The middle argument is the value to find.

functions.SUM: Adds the numbers in a column.
functions.AVERAGE: Average of the numbers. Empty cells are skipped.
functions.COUNT: How many numbers are in the column.
functions.COUNTA: How many cells are not empty.
functions.ROUND: Rounds to the given number of digits.
functions.IF: One value when the condition is true, and another when it is false.
functions.AND: True when every condition is true.
functions.OR: True when any condition is true.
functions.LEFT: The first characters of a text.
functions.RIGHT: The last characters of a text.
functions.LEN: How many characters are in a text.
functions.LOOKUP: Finds a value in one column and returns another column from that row.
